title: Episode 434: Episode 434: Ignaz Semmelweis and Childbed Fever
description:
In the Vienna General Hospital in 1847, young Hungarian obstetrician Ignaz Semmelweis noticed that mothers in the doctors' clinic were dying of puerperal (childbed) fever at five times the rate of mothers in the midwives' clinic. Realizing that doctors were carrying 'cadaverous particles' directly from autopsies to delivery rooms, Semmelweis ordered medical staff to wash their hands in chlorinated lime solution, causing maternal mortality to plummet to near zero. Tragically mocked and ostracized by an arrogant medical establishment, Semmelweis died in a mental asylum before his germ theory was vindicated.
